inference.explanation: The inlet meter is proven, field flows are normal, and the misassigned accounts fully explain the excess. Meters do not create water, and a supply fault was excluded by test.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Investigate the district for a hidden second supply source
Replace the district inlet meter as faulty
Correct the billing boundary file, restate the quarter, and add a boundary check to the audit routine

nextClue.explanation: Fixing the boundary file corrects both districts audits and the routine check prevents recurrence.

clueText.nc-c: The restated quarter balances normally for both districts.
clueText.nc-a: Pressure and flow records show no second source, and the account list explains the gap.
clueText.nc-b: The inlet meter passed its accuracy test the same quarter.

tasks.prompt: A senior operator reviewing three years of audits for a Saskatchewan utility notices real loss per kilometre worsens each year while total real loss stays flat.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional utility that annexed a large low density area in year one. Audit normalization was reviewed at the Class 3 level.

evidence.label: Total real loss volume is the same in all three years.
Kilometres of main grew by 40 percent with the annexation of spread out rural subdivisions.
Loss per service connection improved slightly each year.
Breaks per kilometre fell after annexation because the new mains are new plastic.
Night flow per kilometre in the original city is unchanged.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Leakage intensity is rising across the original city
The per kilometre trend is a denominator effect from annexing long, low density mains, not worsening leakage
The annexed mains leak more per kilometre than old city mains
Crews are finding fewer leaks each year so loss concentrates

inference.explanation: Total loss is flat, the new mains are new with fewer breaks, and original city intensity is unchanged. The ratio moved because the denominator grew with low density pipe.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Report loss per connection and per kilometre for the original and annexed areas separately
Set a single per kilometre target for the combined system
Rank the annexed area first for renewal on the per kilometre figure

nextClue.explanation: Separate reporting keeps the trend honest and stops a ratio artifact from driving renewal money.

clueText.nc-a: Split reporting shows both areas stable, with the annexed area lowest per kilometre.
clueText.nc-b: A combined target would punish the system for geography, not condition.
clueText.nc-c: The annexed mains are the newest in the system with the lowest break rate.

tasks.prompt: A British Columbia senior operator year end review weighs three candidate capital projects against incident history, and the data rank a quiet project first.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional utility year end capital review. Incident, complaint, and cost records for three candidate projects were compiled on one page.

evidence.label: A trunk valve replacement has no incident history but sits on the only feed to a hospital district, and its failure would be severe.
A main renewal candidate has frequent small breaks with modest costs each.
A tank recoating candidate is visible and popular but its condition report shows years of coating life left.
Risk scoring that combines likelihood and consequence puts the valve first by a wide margin.
The valve project is also the cheapest of the three.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The most visible project should rank first for public confidence
Frequent small breaks always outrank a failure that has not happened
Coating condition does not matter if a tank looks tired
Consequence driven risk ranking puts the single feed valve first, ahead of the more visible projects

inference.explanation: Likelihood alone favours the breaks, consequence alone favours the valve, and the combined risk method the utility adopted settles it. Visibility is not a risk factor in any defensible method.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Fund the valve replacement first and record the risk basis so the ranking survives staff changes
Fund the recoating first because it is most visible
Fund the renewal first because its incidents are countable

nextClue.explanation: Recording the basis makes the decision auditable, which is the senior operator standard.

clueText.nc-a: The valve is replaced in the spring outage window without incident.
clueText.nc-b: Public confidence built on a neglected single point of failure is borrowed time.
clueText.nc-c: Countable incidents are only half of a risk score.

tasks.prompt: A loss strategy review in a British Columbia city must choose between city wide pressure reduction and targeted renewal, and the data split sharply by district age.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional city with mixed age districts. Night flow, pressure sensitivity, and break data were compiled per district.

evidence.label: In old districts, leakage falls steeply when night pressure is trialled lower, and breaks are frequent.
In new districts, leakage is already low and barely changes with pressure.
City wide pressure reduction would cut fire flow margins in two high elevation pockets.
Break costs in old districts exceed the cost of the leakage they cause.
A paired trial district held at full pressure shows no leakage change.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: City wide pressure reduction alone is the best single strategy
Renewal alone is best because pressure does nothing for leakage
A combined program fits: pressure management where it is safe, and renewal targeted at the old districts
Neither works, since the trial district showed no change

inference.explanation: Leakage is pressure sensitive where it is high, breaks concentrate in the same old districts, and the high pockets limit a blanket cut. The flat trial district was a control, not proof of no effect.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Apply the pressure cut to the whole city including the high pockets
Pilot pressure management in the old low elevation districts and schedule renewal by break and loss intensity
Renew the newest districts first because access is easier

nextClue.explanation: A phased combined program matches each tool to the districts where the evidence supports it.

clueText.nc-b: After one year, pilot districts cut loss by a quarter with no fire flow complaints.
clueText.nc-a: A blanket cut would breach margins in the high pockets the data flag.
clueText.nc-c: New districts already leak little, so renewing them first saves almost nothing.

tasks.prompt: An Alberta utility weighs acoustic survey frequency: one district surveyed yearly keeps loss low, another surveyed every five years keeps rebounding.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional utility comparing two similar districts over eight years. Survey and repair records are complete for both.

evidence.label: District A, surveyed yearly, holds loss near 10 percent with small repairs each year.
District B, surveyed every five years, drops after each survey then rebounds within two years.
Both districts have similar pipe age, soil, and pressure.
Repair sizes in District B are larger, consistent with leaks running longer before detection.
Survey costs are small beside the treated water value lost in District B rebounds.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: District B mains are made of a worse material than District A
District B customers waste more water between surveys
Surveys themselves cause District B leaks to return
Leak run time drives the difference, so a shorter survey cycle is the cost effective strategy for District B

inference.explanation: The districts match on age, soil, and pressure, and the rebound pattern follows survey timing with larger, longer running leaks. Material and customer explanations have no supporting difference in the records.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Keep the five year cycle and accept the rebound as normal
Survey District B monthly at full program cost
Move District B to a two year survey cycle and track loss rebound after each survey

nextClue.explanation: A two year cycle balances survey cost against the measured rebound loss.

clueText.nc-c: On the shorter cycle, District B loss stabilizes near District A levels.
clueText.nc-a: Eight years of rebounds show the five year cycle loses more water than it saves.
clueText.nc-b: Monthly surveys cost far more than the small leaks they would catch earlier.

tasks.prompt: A Saskatchewan utility must defend a loss budget: council asks why renewal targets one small old district instead of spreading funds across the city.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional utility preparing a capital briefing. District loss intensity and break data were normalized per kilometre.

evidence.label: The small district holds 6 percent of city mains but 31 percent of city real loss.
Its loss per kilometre is five times the city average and its break rate is four times average.
Spreading the same funds city wide would cut total loss by an estimated 4 percent.
Targeting the district is projected to cut total city loss by about 18 percent.
Customer density and pressure are similar across districts.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Concentrating renewal on the high intensity district produces the largest city wide loss reduction
Spreading funds evenly is fairer and cuts loss the most
The small district figures must be a metering error at that scale
Loss follows customer count, so the biggest district should rank first

inference.explanation: Intensity and break data agree, density and pressure are controlled, and the projections follow directly from where the loss sits. Fairness of spread does not change the arithmetic of loss removed per dollar.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Present the per kilometre case to council and phase the district renewal over two years with a loss target
Spread the budget evenly to keep every district equal
Move the funds to the largest district by population

nextClue.explanation: Phased targeted renewal with a published target gives council a measurable result.

clueText.nc-a: Year one renewal removes over half the district excess loss.
clueText.nc-b: Equal spreading was modelled and removes only a fraction of the loss.
clueText.nc-c: Population ranking ignores the measured location of the loss.

tasks.prompt: A Manitoba utility finds its cheapest loss reduction came not from repairs but from fixing pressure transients traced to a booster station.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional utility that logged pressure at high frequency for a year. Break locations and transient events were correlated by the senior team.

evidence.label: High frequency logging shows sharp pressure spikes many times a day downstream of one booster station.
Breaks cluster in the spiked reach and are rare elsewhere at the same pipe age.
A pump control fault causes a hard stop that matches each spike in timing.
After soft start controls are fitted in a trial, spikes disappear and breaks in the reach stop for six months.
Steady state pressure in the reach was never above its rated level.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The reach pipe is simply at end of life and breaks randomly
Transient control, not steady pressure or pipe age, is the priority loss action for this reach
Steady pressure is too high even though gauges read normal
Breaks stopped because winter was milder that year

inference.explanation: Spikes match the pump fault in timing, breaks cluster only in the spiked reach, and the control trial stops both spikes and breaks. Age alone cannot explain why the trial changed the break pattern.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Renew the whole reach before touching the station controls
Fit soft start and surge control at the station permanently and add transient logging to the loss program
Lower steady pressure across the whole zone

nextClue.explanation: Permanent surge control removes the proven break driver at a fraction of renewal cost.

clueText.nc-b: A full year after the fix, the reach has one break against a prior average of nine.
clueText.nc-a: Renewing first would spend capital while the transient driver kept breaking new pipe.
clueText.nc-c: Steady pressure was measured normal, so a zone cut treats the wrong variable.

tasks.prompt: A British Columbia resort town loss strategy must handle demand that triples for ten summer weeks while winter loss percentages look terrible.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional resort town with a small winter population. The strategy review used monthly volumes, not only annual percentages.

evidence.label: Winter supply is low, so a modest fixed leakage volume becomes a high winter percentage.
Summer supply triples and the same leakage volume is a small summer percentage.
Absolute leakage volume is nearly constant across the year.
Night flow in winter equals the summer leakage estimate after resort night use is removed.
No seasonal break pattern exists in the records.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Winter leakage truly triples in volume each year
Summer visitors cause the winter percentage by damaging mains
The town has a steady absolute leakage volume, and strategy should target volume reduction, not the winter percentage
The winter percentage proves the system is failing each winter

inference.explanation: Absolute leakage is constant and night flow confirms it, while percentages swing only because the denominator swings. A true winter volume tripling would appear in night flow and breaks.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Set a winter percentage target equal to the summer percentage
Run detection in mid winter when percentages look worst
Set the loss target in cubic metres per day and run detection in spring before the peak season

nextClue.explanation: A volume target plus pre season detection fits how this system actually loses water.

clueText.nc-c: Spring detection finds and fixes two long running leaks, cutting daily loss volume by a fifth.
clueText.nc-a: A winter percentage target would demand removing more water than the system leaks.
clueText.nc-b: Mid winter work chases a ratio artifact in the hardest working conditions.

tasks.prompt: An Alberta city compares two loss programs on paper: a meter replacement program and a district renewal, and only one is supported by its own audit components.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional city with a component based audit. Apparent and real loss were estimated separately with test data.

evidence.label: Apparent loss from meter testing is estimated at 3 percent of supply.
Real loss from night flow analysis is estimated at 21 percent of supply.
Large meter testing found most large meters within 4 percent of true.
Night flow step tests locate most real loss in two old districts.
The meter program proposal assumes 12 percent apparent loss with no test basis.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Meter replacement should lead because apparent loss is larger
Both programs deserve equal funding regardless of components
The audit components are too uncertain to guide any choice
Renewal and detection in the two old districts should lead, because real loss dominates the measured balance

inference.explanation: Test based components put real loss at seven times apparent loss, and step tests locate it. The meter proposal figure contradicts the city own meter testing.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Fund district detection and renewal first, and keep a routine meter testing program at maintenance scale
Fund the meter program first on the proposal assumption
Split the budget evenly between the two programs

nextClue.explanation: Leading with the dominant, located component removes the most water per dollar.

clueText.nc-a: First year district work cuts real loss by a quarter while meter testing continues routinely.
clueText.nc-b: The proposal assumption of 12 percent was never supported by a test result.
clueText.nc-c: Equal splitting ignores a seven to one difference in measured components.

tasks.prompt: A Saskatchewan First Nations community system, operated with circuit rider support, must choose a first loss action with a small crew and no district metering.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional community system in northern Saskatchewan. Available data are plant production, reservoir levels, and repair records.

evidence.label: Production rises steadily for two years while the serviced population is flat.
Reservoir overnight drop with the community at rest exceeds metered night use estimates by a growing margin.
Repair records show repeated failures on one river crossing feed main.
Acoustic equipment can be borrowed through the circuit rider program for one week.
There is no budget this year for district metering installation.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Start with a borrowed acoustic survey focused on the suspect feed main, using reservoir drop as the baseline measure
Wait until district metering can be funded before any loss work
Replace all services in the community first
Raise production to match the rising trend

inference.explanation: Production, reservoir drop, and repair history all point one way, and a focused survey is achievable with available support. Waiting for ideal metering leaves a growing loss running.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Postpone all action until a full audit can be done
Schedule the borrowed survey on the feed main and track overnight reservoir drop before and after repairs
Begin with a customer meter replacement program

nextClue.explanation: The focused survey plus a simple before and after reservoir measure gives proof with the tools at hand.

clueText.nc-b: The survey finds a crossing leak, and overnight drop falls by a third after repair.
clueText.nc-a: A full audit is not possible without metering, and delay costs treated water daily.
clueText.nc-c: Customer meters were not implicated by any observation in this system.

tasks.prompt: A Manitoba utility loss review finds that reported loss fell for three years only because unbilled municipal use was quietly reclassified each year.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional utility reviewing its own reporting practice. Category definitions in past audits were compared year to year.

evidence.label: Real loss indicators, night flow and breaks, are unchanged over the three years.
Each year, a growing volume of municipal use was moved from loss to authorized use without new metering.
The reclassified volumes were estimates that grew to match the reported improvement exactly.
Flushing and facility use were never metered in any of the three years.
Neighbouring utilities report flat loss on stable definitions.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The utility genuinely cut loss while night flow stayed flat
The reported improvement is a definition drift, and the strategy must restart from metered categories
Reclassification is harmless because the water was really used
Estimates are as good as metering for audit categories

inference.explanation: Physical indicators never moved, and the estimate growth matches the reported gain one for one. Real improvement would show in night flow.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Continue reclassifying to keep the reported trend positive
Report the improvement to the province as a program success
Meter the main municipal uses, freeze category definitions, and restate the three years honestly

nextClue.explanation: Metering plus frozen definitions restores an audit the strategy can actually steer by.

clueText.nc-c: With facilities metered, true authorized use is a third of the estimates used before.
clueText.nc-a: Continuing the drift would steer capital by a fictional trend.
clueText.nc-b: Reporting it as success would misstate performance to the regulator and council.

tasks.prompt: A British Columbia city must set a loss target: its economic analysis shows the cost of finding the last leaks exceeds the value of the water saved.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional city with a completed economic level of leakage study. Marginal detection costs and water production costs were both measured.

evidence.label: At current loss, each further point of reduction costs more in survey and repair than the water is worth in production cost.
Loss is already below the level where bursts and background leakage balance detection cost.
The study used the city own production cost, not a borrowed figure.
Pressure is already managed and large leaks are found quickly by telemetry alarms.
No regulatory requirement in the province sets a lower numeric loss target for this system.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Drive loss to near zero whatever the detection cost
Let loss rise until bursts force action
Hold loss near the current economic level and spend the marginal dollar on renewal of high break mains instead
Copy a lower target from a city with cheaper detection costs

inference.explanation: The study is built on local costs, pressure and detection are already strong, and no numeric mandate applies. Near zero loss would spend more than the water saved is worth.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Adopt the economic level as the target and redirect the surplus budget to break driven renewal
Set a zero loss target for the next plan period
Adopt the other city target unchanged

nextClue.explanation: An economic target with renewal redirection is the defensible Class 3 strategy this evidence supports.

clueText.nc-a: Two years at the target hold loss steady while break driven renewal cuts emergency repairs.
clueText.nc-b: Zero loss is not achievable at any reasonable cost in a buried network.
clueText.nc-c: Another city target reflects its costs, not this system economics.
